target_customer: Families, especially those with long distance relatives, who wanted a private place to share updates and photos
problem: Facebook was public and cluttered for family sharing, and older family sites were dated, so families lacked a simple private hub.
business_model: Free consumer social network at launch with no revenue model stated

founders.name: Wesley Zhao
founders.background_notes: Childhood friend of Ajay Mehta; earlier made a Y U NO yarn pitch that helped them into YC.

founders.name: Ajay Mehta
founders.background_notes: Joined Crowdtilt after the sale per TechCrunch; YC page bio lists Portola, Birthdate Co. and Therapy Notebooks.

founders.name: Henry Liu
founders.background_notes: Listed on the YC page; TechCrunch 2013 says he worked with YC backed Verbling after the sale.

founders.name: Brandon Paton
founders.background_notes: Listed on the YC page; TechCrunch says he left before the acquisition.

exit.reason: Origami bought the one modern competitor; FamilyLeaf was wound down, users offered an import tool, and part of the investor cash was returned.

competitors.name: Facebook
competitors.what: General social network families already used

technical_complexity.rationale: Private pages, photo import from Facebook, Instagram, Flickr and Picasa via Chute, email posting and seven translations are ordinary web work for two students.

defensibility.rationale: Value only grows per family, there was no cross family network effect, and the product was copyable; competitors named were already in the space.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No incumbent bought it; a YC competitor, Origami Labs, acquired it in Jul 2013 and Origami itself was sold to eFamily in Nov 2013.

market_need_then: TechCrunch in Mar 2012 said it resonated with people with many long distance relatives; the founder ran three family networks across the US, Europe and India.

branding.domain_note: Used familyleaf.com, the exact .com; Origami later offered users a familyleaf.com subdomain after the sale.

identity.voice_and_tone: Warm, family focused mission statement about bringing families closer

branding.community_and_virality: Founders drew press for a Y U NO themed pitch and a public YC application discussed on Hacker News; no merch or fan community found.

brand_strength.rationale: A clear and friendly name, but only founder driven press coverage and a small base of about 7,500 families.

outcome_analysis: FamilyLeaf reached about 7,500 families in over 150 countries, 35 percent active, but had no revenue model and only modest seed money. In Jul 2013 Origami Labs bought it and the team moved on with no jobs offered, part of the investor cash being returned. It was a soft landing where the product was wound down.
notes: Batch conflict: YC lists Winter 2012, TechCrunch says Spring 2012. Funding figures conflict: CB Insights says about 20K, Company Check 177K over 2 rounds, Wellfound 984K across rounds with Y Combinator, SV Angel and Kevin Carter; all aggregator only and unverified. TechCrunch (2013) names YC, Start Fund (167K) and an undisclosed amount from 500 Startups and others; the Start Fund amount is recorded as the only round with a stated figure and its date 2012 is inferred from the seed timing, not stated. Company site familyleaf.com could not be fetched (DNS error). Exit amount undisclosed.
